request.contents:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: On signing, the Tenant shall give the Landlord a signed blank cheque, to be kept as security and returned uncashed when the tenancy ends.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
Under the Ontario *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006* (RTA), a landlord is strictly prohibited from demanding or accepting any form of security deposit other than a rent deposit (typically known as the "last month's rent" deposit), which cannot exceed the amount of rent for one rent period.

Section 105(1) of the RTA states:
> "The only security deposit that a landlord may collect is a rent deposit collected in accordance with section 106."

Furthermore, section 1(1) of the RTA defines a "security deposit" broadly as "money, property or a right paid or given by, or on behalf of, a tenant of a rental unit to a landlord or to anyone on the landlord’s behalf to be held by or for the landlord as security for the performance of an obligation or the payment of a liability of the tenant or to be returned to the tenant upon the happening of a condition." 

Because a signed blank cheque held as security to be returned at the end of the tenancy falls directly under the definition of a security deposit and is not a valid rent deposit collected in accordance with section 106, demanding or collecting it is prohibited under section 105. (By extension, under section 4 of the RTA, any provision in a tenancy agreement that conflicts with the Act is void.)

Verdict: not enforceable
Section: 105
